title_en: Interim Provisions on Import Taxation of Articles Carried by Foreign Permanent Residents in China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Provisions are formulated for the purpose of implementing the policy of opening to the outside world, enhancing foreign exchanges, and promoting the development of foreign economic trade.

Article 3 For the six categories of resident personnel mentioned above who have resided in China for more than one year (i.e., whose validity period of work or study visa exceeds one year), with respect to personal household video cameras, cameras, portable radio-cassette recorders, portable laser disc players, and portable computers that they bring into China for the first time during the validity period of their visa for personal use, upon declaration to and verification by the competent customs office at the place of residence, and within the quantity limit of one unit per product type, such articles shall be exempted from import duties; the portion exceeding the limit shall be subject to taxation in accordance with relevant regulations.

Article 4 For foreign experts (including experts from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) or overseas Chinese experts who meet the conditions stipulated in Article 2, the import duties on books, data, scientific research instruments, tools, samples, reagents, and other teaching and research articles brought into China by them shall be exempted within the scope of reasonable quantities for personal use.

Article 5 For baggage and articles other than those specified in Articles 3 and 4 that are brought into China by the foreign personnel mentioned above during their stay in China for living, study, or work purposes, the matter shall be governed by the Regulations of the Customs of the People's Republic of China on the Supervision and Control of Baggage and Articles of Inbound and Outbound Passengers.
Article 6 The duty-free articles imported under the provisions above shall be subject to customs supervision in accordance with the relevant regulations of the customs on duty-free imported articles.

Article 7 The articles brought into China by resident personnel (including their accompanying spouses and minor children who come to reside in China) of diplomatic missions and consular posts of foreign countries (including regions) in China, as well as of specialized agencies of the United Nations and permanent representative offices of international organizations, shall still be governed by the current relevant provisions.
Article 8 Any previous policies and provisions that are inconsistent with these Provisions shall be governed by these Provisions.
Article 9 The General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China shall, pursuant to these Provisions, formulate implementing rules.
Article 10 These Provisions shall come into force as of April 1, 1999.
